Latvia and Its Current Economy

Latvia is a member of the European Union and possesses an open economy in the northern part of Europe. The current economy of Latvia is pretty stable and after the event of Brexit, it did not sustain any major threat. Though several scientists predict that in the long run Brexit may cast an impact upon Latvia’s economy, as there is a good chance that it may decrease the overall economic growth of the entire EU. The current IT industry of Latvia is pretty vibrant even after Brexit. But there is a good chance that it might be sustaining a few damages eventually. Here we are discussing the reasons to hire dedicated developers in Latvia.

Outsourcing Is Hot – Latvia Developers for Hire

Over the past few years, different individuals, as well as companies, have been outsourcing different kinds of IT related projects to people residing in other countries. Baltic countries became a popular destination for software development outsourcing. Many European countries consider as a good idea to hire developers in Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia. Just like the rest of the world, Latvia has also been outsourcing its IT projects to offshore companies for the past few years, but the trends for this country are changing now. Being one of the Soviet countries, Latvia remains quite competitive in terms of offering quality development services to other countries of the European Union at a very affordable rate. Since Latvia joined EU only in 2014, demands from Latvian developers here are not so high. Average salary within the country remains quite low comparing to other European countries, Latvia is currently ranked as #24 (out of 28) in the List of European countries by average wage. At the same time, the average salary grew by 20.77% within last 3 years, which points at steady economics growth.

Latvia’s English Proficiency Index score of 571, signifying “High Proficiency,” underscores the nation’s commendable command of the English language, bolstering its global communication and economic competitiveness.

An Overview of the IT Industry in Latvia

Latvia has a vibrant IT industry that is expanding at a rapid pace. The sector of software development in Latvia is vital to the country’s overall economic development, with an exceptional growth rate of 8.72%. Latvia has roughly 2,200 IT companies, showing an active and competitive business environment. These organizations employ over 39,000 IT experts, demonstrating the sector’s importance in creating job opportunities and the ongoing need to hire backend engineers. Latvia’s technology industry export value is an outstanding $1.94 billion, demonstrating the sector’s significant global presence. 

According to the Latvian programming language market share as of July 2023, PHP has the highest share with 49.59% of clients, making it the most popular language in the country. Microsoft ASP.NET has a 1.52% market share, following PHP, while Python and Perl have 1.15% and 0.21%, respectively. Ruby and Java finish the list with 0.18% and 0.17% of the market share, indicating their growing but still fairly minor presence in Latvian IT companies.

A Look at The Employment Conditions in Latvia

Latvia’s employment conditions reflect a diverse economy. Key sectors are manufacturing, IT and agriculture. The country has fostered a significant focus on international trade. This has contributed to the growth of many different industries and enhanced job prospects. The labor market is characterized by quite a skilled workforce and a growing emphasis on innovation and technology, driving the country’s economic development.

Payroll cycles in Latvia adhere to a monthly payment schedule, with salaries commonly disbursed at the end of each month. Employers must, of course, follow with specific payroll taxes! For example, contributions towards social security, healthcare and other statutory benefits. 

The minimum wage in Latvia’s seen gradual increases in recent years. And, currently, it stands at approximately $660 per month. Overtime pay is overseen by labor laws, ensuring that employees receive additional money for any extra hours worked.

Employee benefits are an essential aspect of the employment framework in Latvia. Many companies offer comprehensive health insurance, paid leave and retirement plans to their workforce.

IT Hubs in Latvia

The salary of software developers in Latvia can vary widely depending on factors such as the developer’s level of expertise, the difficulty of their work, the size of their employer, and the location of Latvia IT companies office.

  • Riga: The largest capital city of Latvia, is where software engineers may expect to get the best pay. Average monthly gross salaries are about €2,421 for middle software developers.
  • Daugavpils: The country’s second-largest city is home to a thriving IT sector. Software engineers may expect to make between €1,500 and €4,000 per month, on average, in gross pay.
  • Liepāja: Acity noted for its cultural and sporting activities. As for the IT sector, for example, web development company Latvia can offer a gross monthly pay of around €2,350 for middle-level specialists.
  • Jelgava: Jelgava, located in central Latvia, is home to a great tech-specialized Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies, which may impact the local IT job market. Salary ranges for software developers typically range from €981 to €1,431 per month.
  • Jūrmala:  Being mostly a vacation destination, Jūrmala may not have as many IT career prospects as the other cities. The salary for software developers in this city is typically €1,519, but the number of vacancies is quite low.

The average software developer salary Riga is about €1,840 per month. There are many new kinds of legislation and human resource recruiting laws, which offer financial benefits for the companies to offer reduced prices to global clients. The quality of software development in Latvia is very high.

Legal and Regulatory Aspects of Hiring and Employment in Latvia

While Latvia and Ukraine have legislative frameworks in place for recruiting processes and intellectual property protection, understanding the particular complexities of these regulations is critical when you want to hire dedicated developers Latvia or Ukraine. 

Hiring Process: Legal Implications in Latvia and Ukraine

Both Latvia and Ukraine have laws in place to guarantee an inclusive and nondiscriminatory hiring environment. While Ukraine is not a member of the European Union, its labor rules generally align with the EU’s.

The Labor Law and the Law on the Prevention of Discrimination govern the hiring process in Latvia. All applicants should be evaluated fairly regarding their experience, education, and other relevant factors. Those not citizens of the European Union need first get a work visa or a residency permit that grants them the ability to work. EU residents often do not need a work permit to work in Latvia. Still, they might have to register their address and follow other laws. Within the first month of employment, the employer must provide the employee with a written employment contract.

The legal framework for the selection process in Ukraine is laid forth in the Constitution and the Labor Code. Like Latvia, Ukraine forbids discrimination based on a person’s race, color, religion, political affiliation, national or ethnic origin, etc. The employment agreement needs to be presented on the first day of work. Foreign nationals may need special authorization to work in Ukraine legally.

IP Protection: Understanding the Legal Framework in Both Countries

Intellectual Property is protected by law in both Latvia and Ukraine.

As a member of the European Union, Latvia has strict regulations to protect the developer’s rights to their work. The Latvian Patent Office ensures these rules are followed so inventors can fully own their works.

Ukraine has its own unique set of rules and regulations. Despite the standards’ existence and the influence of different international organizations, enforcing them can be difficult. However, Ukraine has taken steps to protect intellectual property better, making the country an increasingly secure environment for IT professionals.

The average salary of Riga developer is equal to  $55,000 per year. Front-end developers in Riga can earn $3,000 monthly while their colleagues in Kyiv have $2,500 for the same skills. Back-end developers in Riga and Kyiv have $7,000 and $2700 accordingly. Middle-level full-stack programmers from Riga have $7,500 in a month. It is still less than developers’ salaries in the USA but Kyiv, Ukraine seems to be the more advantageous city in the terms of costs, which makes hiring SW development engineer in Ukraine advantageous.
